(as ''Racing Club de Strasbourg'')}} | stadium = [[Stade de la Meinau]] | capacity = 32,300 | owner = [[BlueCo]] | chairman = [[Marc Keller]] | chrtitle = President | manager = [[Hugo Oliveira (football manager)|Hugo Oliveira]] | mgrtitle = Head coach | league = {{French football updater|Strasbourg}} | season = {{French football updater|Strasbourg2}} | position = {{French football updater|Strasbourg3}} | website = {{Official URL}} | pattern_la1 = _strasbourg2627h | pattern_b1 = _strasbourg2627h | pattern_ra1 = _strasbourg2627h | pattern_sh1 = _strasbourg2627h | pattern_so1 = _socks | leftarm1 = 0000DD | body1 = 0000DD | rightarm1 = 0000DD | shorts1 = FFFFFF | socks1 = 0000DD | pattern_la2 = _strasbourg2627a | pattern_b2 = _strasbourg2627a | pattern_ra2 = _strasbourg2627a | pattern_sh2 = _strasbourg2627a | pattern_so2 = _socks | leftarm2 = FAF7F0 | body2 = FAF7F0 | rightarm2 = FAF7F0 | shorts2 = FAF7F0 | socks2 = FAF7F0 | pattern_la3 = _strasbourg2627t | pattern_b3 = _strasbourg2627t | pattern_ra3 = _strasbourg2627t | pattern_sh3 = _strasbourg2627t | pattern_so3 = _monterrey1213t1 | leftarm3 = | body3 = | rightarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = 000000 | current = 2026–27 RC Strasbourg Alsace season }} '''Racing Club de Strasbourg Alsace''', commonly known as '''RC Strasbourg''' ({{langx|gsw|RC Stroßburg}}, {{langx|de|RC Straßburg}}; '''RCS''') or simply just '''Racing''', is a [[football in France|French professional association football]] club founded in 1906 and based in the city of [[Strasbourg]], [[Alsace]]. It became a professional club in 1933, and is currently playing in [[Ligue 1]], the top tier of [[Football in France|French football]], having won the [[2016–17 Ligue 2]] championship. This comes after the club was demoted to the fifth tier of French football at the conclusion of the [[2010–11 Championnat National]] season after going into financial liquidation. Renamed '''RC Strasbourg Alsace''', they won the CFA championship in 2012–13, and became Championnat National champions in 2015–16. [[Stade de la Meinau]] has been the club's stadium since 1914. RC Strasbourg is one of twelve clubs to have won all three major French trophies: Division 1, now [[Ligue 1]], in [[1978–79 French Division 1|1979]]; the [[Coupe de France]] in [[1951 Coupe de France Final|1951]], [[1965–66 Coupe de France|1966]] and [[2000–01 Coupe de France|2001]]; and the [[Coupe de la Ligue]] in 1964, [[1997 Coupe de la Ligue Final|1997]], [[2004–05 Coupe de la Ligue|2005]] and [[2018–19 Coupe de la Ligue|2019]]. It is also among the thirteen teams to have played more than 2,000 games in France's top flight (spanning 67 seasons){{cite web|url=http://lfp.fr/ligue1/historique/bilanClubFrancais.asp |title=Ligue de Football Professionnel : Ligue 1, actualités, résultats, classements, statistiques |publisher=Lfp.fr |access-date=19 November 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080822124801/http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/historique/bilanClubFrancais.asp |archive-date=22 August 2008 |url-status=dead}} and has taken part in 52 European games since 1961.{{cite web|url=http://lfp.fr/coupeEurope/bilanClubFrancais.asp |title=Ligue de Football Professionnel : Coupe UEFA, Coupes d'Europe, Coupe de France, Ligue des Champions |publisher=Lfp.fr |access-date=19 November 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081217044825/http://www.lfp.fr/coupeEurope/bilanClubFrancais.asp |archive-date=17 December 2008 }} By contrast, it has also experienced relegation at least once a decade since the early 1950s. It has changed its manager 52 times in 75 years of professional play. The destiny of the RC Strasbourg has always been wedded to the [[Alsace#History|history of Alsace]]. Like the region, the club has changed nationality three times and has a troubled history. The club was founded when the city (and the region of Alsace-Lorraine) was part of the [[German Empire]], and the club insisted on its Alsatian and popular roots from the beginning, in opposition to the first Strasbourg-based clubs which came from the German-born bourgeoisie. When Alsace was returned to France after the [[World War I|First World War]], the club changed its name from 1. FC Neudorf to the current Racing Club de Strasbourg, in imitation of [[Pierre de Coubertin]]'s [[Racing Club de France football Colombes 92|Racing Club de France]], a clear gesture of [[Francophile|Francophilia]]. RC Strasbourg players lived through the [[World War II|Second World War]] as most Alsatians did: evacuated in 1939, annexed in 1940 and striving to avoid Nazification and incorporation in the [[Wehrmacht]] between 1942 and 1944. When Alsace was definitively returned to France after the war, Strasbourg's identity switched towards [[Jacobin (politics)|Jacobinism]] with, for example, emotional wins in the cup in 1951 and 1966 amidst Franco-Alsatian controversies."}}
